split_reasoning: Assigning duties and responsibilities is one activity with a common output: a project work assignment.

split_reasoning: Determining requirements and objectives through stakeholder communication is one interactive activity.

split_reasoning: Identifying and resolving problems through discussions with project personnel is one interactive activity.

parts.type_reasoning: The work described is a live discussion to diagnose and agree on responses to problems.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Problem discussions may occur in project meetings or lead to plan changes, but neither is required for every discussion.

split_reasoning: Creating a project status presentation is one deliverable regardless of its audience.

split_reasoning: Developing or updating a project plan is one activity; the listed topics are components of the same plan.

split_reasoning: Identifying resource, staffing, and financial needs is one assessment using project objectives and schedules as inputs.

parts.unit_reasoning: A needs assessment for a project or planning cycle is a usable output, rather than each individual resource estimate.

parts.end: resource, staffing, and financial needs are identified and communicated or recorded

split_reasoning: Identifying, reviewing, and selecting vendors or consultants are stages of the same sourcing decision.

split_reasoning: Cost monitoring is continuous but produces individual budget issues for investigation or escalation.

split_reasoning: Continuous milestone and deliverable monitoring can be represented by individual tracked milestone or deliverable status updates.

parts.text: Check and update the status of a project milestone or deliverable.

split_reasoning: Monitoring performance can produce a documented assessment, while delivering feedback is a separate live interaction.

parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment of one team member for a review period or feedback occasion is a coherent item.

parts.end: observations are recorded or prepared for feedback

parts.text: Give a project team member performance feedback.
parts.type_reasoning: The value of feedback is in the live discussion with the team member.
parts.overlap_reasoning: A feedback discussion can address project problems, but problem-solving discussions need not be performance feedback.

notes: Feedback may be informal and not accompanied by a separate written assessment; shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: Negotiating with stakeholders or suppliers is one activity aimed at obtaining project resources or materials.

parts.overlap_reasoning: Supplier selection may precede negotiation, but evaluating candidates and negotiating terms are not the same work.

split_reasoning: Planning, scheduling, and coordinating activities are related steps in arranging project work to meet deadlines.

parts.end: the sequence and timing are recorded or communicated to participants

parts.text: Prepare and submit a project cost tracking report.

split_reasoning: Proposing a plan modification and reviewing or approving a proposed modification are distinct activities with different outputs.

split_reasoning: Recruiting candidates and making a hire are distinct activities with different outputs.

split_reasoning: Project status is reported both in written updates and in live discussions with managers.

split_reasoning: Requesting and reviewing a project update are steps in checking progress against deadlines.
